title: Microfluidic encapsulation of Xenopus laevis cell-free extracts using hydrogel photolithography
protocol: Remove device from ddH2O and dab any droplets of water off the device.
Clean the coverslip surface gently with a laboratory napkin and 100% ethanol.
Mix 30 channel volumes of PEGDA solution using a syringe and a 22 G blunt needle.
Leave the device full after mixing.
Dab away excess solution from the outlet.
Select either inlet for the step.
Move the filled device onto the stage of an inverted microscope in a room with minimal ambient light.
Choose the desired exposure conditions based on the hydrogel-forming solution stoichiometry and digital mask for photo-patterning.
Begin patterning the coverslip surface using the DMD.
Add a fiduciary mark to the PDMS side of the coverslip outside the chamber.
Pattern the coverslip with a desired micro-structure.
Prime the microbore tubing with buffer at a high flow rate until a droplet forms at the end.
Inspect the length of tubing for any bubbles after priming.
Insert microbore tubing into the outlet opposite the PEGDA microstructures.
Run a flow of ∼5–10 μL/min through the tubing.
Flush out unpolymerized PEGDA solution with 50 channel volumes of CSF-XB buffer.
Flush the channel with buffer.
Remove the microbore tubing carefully.
Store the device at 4°C submerged in CSF-XB buffer until use.
Place the PDMS device near the syringe pump in a 4°C cold room.
Dab any excess buffer from the top of the PDMS device.
Begin flushing device with cell-free extract.
Insert microbore tubing in the inlet nearest the hydrogel microstructures.
Pump 50 channel volumes of extract through the device at 7 μL/min.
Dab away fluid from the opposite port after flushing.
Remove the microbore tubing carrying extract using forceps.
Insert the microbore tubing from the syringe containing encapsulation oil and surfactant into the inlet opposite of hydrogel structures.
Insert microbore tubing securely into the opposite port.
Begin flushing the channel with encapsulation oil at a rate of ∼20–25 μL/min for short pulses (around 5 μL increments).
Separate each pulse by 5 s and repeat three times in total.
Remove tubing carefully using forceps.
Dab away any remaining oil and extract from the top of the PDMS device.
Seal inlets with small sections of tubing tied with an overhand knot.
Clean salts or compounds dried on the bottom of the coverslip with 100% ethanol.
Move the device to a temperature-controlled room for imaging.
